name: Shared Storage API (retired)
plain: Cross-site storage whose values could only be read in a locked worker. Retired Oct 2025.
meaning: Let scripts write cross-site values (for example a frequency count) and read them only inside a worklet that output through limited channels (selectURL, Private Aggregation). Disabled starting build 153.0.8001.0; code removal follows.

access.persistence: Entries expire after 30 days, renewable on write
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

data.metric: Key/value pairs readable in worklet only

limits.headline: Can't store cross site data for ads in Chrome anymore, since it was retired in 2025
limits.user_action: Nothing. It used to happen in the background on pages with embedded ads
can: Have stored values in the browser that any site could use through a locked worker
Have helped choose an ad or count reach without naming you
cannot: Work in Edge, Firefox or Safari
Show stored values to the page directly
Replace cookies for all ad needs

story.what_it_is: Chrome storage that held cross site values in a locked room. Retired.

marketing.name: Shared Storage API
marketing.pitch: Chrome pitched it as unpartitioned storage that could be read only in a locked worklet with limited outputs.

story.for_you: You never saw it. A script could write a value, such as a count, that other sites could read only inside a locked worker. Chrome is turning it off. You will not meet it.
story.for_makers: It was meant to help with things like frequency capping and A/B tests without tracking. Reads had to go through limited paths. With the Privacy Sandbox ad parts retired, it is going away.

use_cases.example: An ad network counted how many times you saw an ad across sites to avoid showing it too often.
A test tool used it to keep the same A or B design across sites you visit.
A game studio could cap how often it showed the same promo across sites.
A publisher used it to pick which ad creative to show without a profile.
A retailer used it to know a visitor saw a sale ad on a partner site.
A social login widget could have stored a flag across sites, read only in a safe room.

technical_bounds: selectURL leaks log2(n) bits capped at about 12 bits per 24 hours per top-level site (budget)
No direct script access to values

history.change: Retirement announced (Private Aggregation including Shared Storage)
Disabled from 153.0.8001.0, code removal without staged rollout (post dated Sep 30 2026)
